meta.examples_note: Provisional selection from correct annotations; may change. Swap an example by replacing it with one of alternatives_record_indices. The UI must stay fully data-driven.

provenance_values.annotated: NLQ object from the authors' human annotation, judged correct
provenance_values.logged: copied from real ABISS run logs (trace, dialogue or NLQ object)
provenance_values.illustrative: hand-written placeholder, must be replaced before the paper/video

examples_selection.rule: Annotator_1 records where every applicable quality flag is true, question_type matches the category type, disambiguation does not change meaning; realism is not required for Improper Question (as in the paper).
examples_selection.single_db_note: No single DB covers more than 6 of 13 subcategories with correct annotations; minimum cover needs 4 DBs. Missing Relationships has only one correct record (thrombosis_prediction).

subcategories.name: Without Evidence
subcategories.definition: The question maps to exactly one SQL query on D without any external evidence.

subcategories.name: With Evidence
subcategories.definition: The question maps to exactly one SQL query on D only when the evidence in K is used.

subcategories.name: Scope Ambiguity
subcategories.definition: Unclear quantifiers (each, every, all) admit a collective or a distributive reading.

subcategories.name: Attachment Ambiguity
subcategories.definition: It is unclear how a modifier attaches within the sentence.

subcategories.name: Lexical Overlap
subcategories.definition: Two or more schema attributes share similar or identical forms.

subcategories.name: Entity Ambiguity
subcategories.definition: Multiple plausible entities could satisfy the same reference.

subcategories.name: Lexical Vagueness
subcategories.definition: A term lacks a precise or objective boundary, leading to vague selection criteria.

subcategories.name: Missing User Knowledge
subcategories.definition: A user-anchored expression (my, our, me, I) needs a user-specific fact absent from D and K.

subcategories.name: Conflicting Knowledge
subcategories.definition: K contains multiple non-equivalent pieces of evidence for the same concept.

subcategories.name: Missing Entities or Attributes
subcategories.definition: Key information (tables or columns) is absent from the schema.

subcategories.name: Missing Relationships
subcategories.definition: The required entities exist but no linkage between them is represented.

subcategories.name: Missing External Knowledge
subcategories.definition: Interpretation depends on objective domain facts or policies not in D or K.

subcategories.name: Improper Question
subcategories.definition: The question is unrelated to the domain of D or K, or is not a database query.

validation_stages.name: Placeholder check
validation_stages.notes: Removes a candidate whose question, hidden knowledge or feedback is a copy of the output template.

validation_stages.name: Duplicate removal
validation_stages.notes: Removes a candidate that repeats a kept question on the same database: the same text, or the same SQL template with the same hidden knowledge.

validation_stages.name: SQL executability
validation_stages.notes: The ground-truth SQL must run in time and return data, and the two interpretations of an ambiguous question must give different results.

validation_stages.name: Category conformance
validation_stages.notes: The council judges whether the question belongs to its subcategory.
validation_stages.vote_meaning: Yes: the question belongs to its category.
validation_stages.decision: Kept when the counted Yes votes outnumber the No votes; a tie removes. The vote of the model that wrote the question does not count.

validation_stages.name: Ground truth satisfaction
validation_stages.notes: The council judges whether the ground-truth SQL answers the question.
validation_stages.vote_meaning: Yes: the ground-truth SQL answers the question.
validation_stages.decision: Kept when the counted Yes votes outnumber the No votes; a tie removes. The vote of the model that wrote the question does not count.

validation_stages.name: Evidence necessity
validation_stages.notes: Each council model writes SQL without the evidence. If one reaches the reference result, the evidence was not needed.
validation_stages.vote_meaning: True: the model's query gives the reference result without the evidence.
validation_stages.decision: Removed when one counted model reaches the reference. The vote of the model that wrote the question does not count.

vote_labels.true: reached the reference without the evidence

validation_stages.name: Information sufficiency
validation_stages.notes: Each council model writes SQL with the evidence and the hidden knowledge of the interpretation. The information must be enough to reach the reference result.
validation_stages.vote_meaning: True: the model's query gives the reference result.
validation_stages.decision: Kept when a model that did not write the question reaches the reference.

validation_stages.name: Unsolvability verification
validation_stages.notes: Each council model tries to write SQL for the unanswerable question, and the council judges each query that runs and returns data.
validation_stages.vote_meaning: True: the council accepted this model's query as an answer to the question.
validation_stages.decision: Removed when the query of one counted model is accepted. The vote of the model that wrote the question does not count.

validation_stages.name: Feedback quality
validation_stages.notes: The council judges whether the feedback correctly explains why the question cannot be answered.
validation_stages.decision: Kept when the counted Yes votes outnumber the No votes; a tie removes. The vote of the model that wrote the question does not count.

validation_stages.name: Category consistency
validation_stages.notes: The question's subcategory is compared with every other subcategory of the same kind.
validation_stages.vote_meaning: 0: the own category wins the comparison. 1: the other category wins, confirmed with the order swapped.
validation_stages.decision: Kept when the own category wins a strict majority of the counted votes against every other category. The vote of the model that wrote the question does not count.

validation_stages.name: Style conformance
validation_stages.notes: The council judges whether the question is written in its style.
validation_stages.vote_meaning: Yes: the question matches its style.
validation_stages.decision: Kept when the counted Yes votes outnumber the No votes; a tie removes. The vote of the model that wrote the question does not count.

category_modes.label: Predicted
category_modes.system_sees: its own guess of the subcategory

tables.name: schools

columns.name: NCESDist
columns.description: National Center for Educational Statistics school district identification number. This field represents the 7-digit National Center for Educational Statistics (NCES) school district identification number. The first 2 digits identify the state and the last 5 digits identify the school district. Combined, they make a unique 7-digit ID for each school district.

columns.name: NCESSchool
columns.description: National Center for Educational Statistics school identification number. This field represents the 5-digit NCES school identification number. The NCESSchool combined with the NCESDist form a unique 12-digit ID for each school.

columns.name: StatusType
columns.description: This field identifies the status of the district.. Values: Definitions of the valid status types are listed below: · Active: The district is in operation and providing instructional services. · Closed: The district is not in operation and no longer providing instructional services. · Merged: The district has combined with another district or districts. · Pending: The district has not opened for operation and instructional services yet, but plans to open within the next 9–12 months.

columns.name: County
columns.description: County name

columns.name: StreetAbr
columns.description: street address. The abbreviated street address of the school, district, or administrative authority’s physical location.. Values: The abbreviated street address of the school, district, or administrative authority’s physical location. Note: Some records (primarily records of closed or retired schools) may not have data in this field.

columns.name: MailStreet
columns.description: Values: The unabbreviated mailing address of the school, district, or administrative authority. Note: 1) Some entities (primarily closed or retired schools) may not have data in this field; 2) Many active entities have not provided a mailing street address. For your convenience we have filled the unpopulated MailStreet cells with Street data.

columns.name: MailStrAbr
columns.description: mailing street address. Values: the abbreviated mailing street address of the school, district, or administrative authority.Note: Many active entities have not provided a mailing street address. For your convenience we have filled the unpopulated MailStrAbr cells with StreetAbr data.

columns.name: MailCity
columns.description: mailing city. Values: The city associated with the mailing address of the school, district, or administrative authority. Note: Many entities have not provided a mailing address city. For your convenience we have filled the unpopulated MailCity cells with City data.

columns.name: MailZip
columns.description: mailing zip. Values: The zip code associated with the mailing address of the school, district, or administrative authority. Note: Many entities have not provided a mailing address zip code. For your convenience we have filled the unpopulated MailZip cells with Zip data.

columns.name: MailState
columns.description: mailing state. Values: The state within the mailing address. For your convenience we have filled the unpopulated MailState cells with State data.

columns.name: Ext
columns.description: extension. The phone number extension of the school, district, or administrative authority.. Values: The phone number extension of the school, district, or administrative authority.

columns.name: Website
columns.description: The website address of the school, district, or administrative authority.. Values: The website address of the school, district, or administrative authority.

columns.name: OpenDate
columns.description: The date the school opened.

columns.name: ClosedDate
columns.description: The date the school closed.

columns.name: Charter
columns.description: This field identifies a charter school.. Values: The field is coded as follows: · 1 = The school is a charter · 0 = The school is not a charter

columns.name: CharterNum
columns.description: The charter school number,. Values: 4-digit number assigned to a charter school.

columns.name: FundingType
columns.description: Indicates the charter school funding type. Values: Values are as follows: · Not in CS (California School) funding model · Locally funded · Directly funded

columns.name: DOC
columns.description: District Ownership Code. Values: The District Ownership Code (DOC) is the numeric code used to identify the category of the Administrative Authority. 00 - County Office of Education 02 – State Board of Education 03 – Statewide Benefit Charter 31 – State Special Schools 34 – Non-school Location* 52 – Elementary School District 54 – Unified School District 56 – High School District 98 – Regional Occupational Center/Program (ROC/P) commonsense evidence: *Only the California Education Authority has been included in the non-school location category.

columns.name: DOCType
columns.description: The District Ownership Code Type. The District Ownership Code Type is the text description of the DOC category.. Values: (See text values in DOC field description above)

columns.name: SOC
columns.description: School Ownership Code. The School Ownership Code is a numeric code used to identify the type of school.. Values: 08 - Preschool 09 – Special Education Schools (Public) 11 – Youth Authority Facilities (CEA) 13 – Opportunity Schools 14 – Juvenile Court Schools 15 – Other County or District Programs 31 – State Special Schools 60 – Elementary School (Public) 61 – Elementary School in 1 School District (Public) 62 – Intermediate/Middle Schools (Public) 63 – Alternative Schools of Choice 64 – Junior High Schools (Public) 65 – K-12 Schools (Public) 66 – High Schools (Public) 67 – High Schools in 1 School District (Public) 68 – Continuation High Schools 69 – District Community Day Schools 70 – Adult Education Centers 98 – Regional Occupational Center/Program (ROC/P)

columns.name: SOCType
columns.description: School Ownership Code Type. The School Ownership Code Type is the text description of the type of school.. Values: The School Ownership Code Type is the text description of the type of school.

columns.name: EdOpsCode
columns.description: Education Option Code. The Education Option Code is a short text description of the type of education offered.. Values: ALTSOC – Alternative School of Choice COMM – County Community School COMMDAY – Community Day School CON – Continuation School JUV – Juvenile Court School OPP – Opportunity School YTH – Youth Authority School SSS – State Special School SPEC – Special Education School TRAD – Traditional ROP – Regional Occupational Program HOMHOS – Home and Hospital SPECON – District Consortia Special Education School

columns.name: EdOpsName
columns.description: Educational Option Name. Values: The Educational Option Name is the long text description of the type of education being offered.

columns.name: EILCode
columns.description: Educational Instruction Level Code. The Educational Instruction Level Code is a short text description of the institution's type relative to the grade range served.. Values: A – Adult ELEM – Elementary ELEMHIGH – Elementary-High Combination HS – High School INTMIDJR – Intermediate/Middle/Junior High PS – Preschool UG – Ungraded

columns.name: EILName
columns.description: Educational Instruction Level Name. The Educational Instruction Level Name is the long text description of the institution’s type relative to the grade range served.. Values: The Educational Instruction Level Name is the long text description of the institution’s type relative to the grade range served.

columns.name: GSoffered
columns.description: grade span offered. The grade span offered is the lowest grade and the highest grade offered or supported by the school, district, or administrative authority. This field might differ from the grade span served as reported in the most recent certified California Longitudinal Pupil Achievement (CALPADS) Fall 1 data collection.. Values: For example XYZ School might display the following data: GSoffered = P–Adult GSserved = K–12

columns.name: GSserved
columns.description: grade span served.. It is the lowest grade and the highest grade of student enrollment as reported in the most recent certified CALPADS Fall 1 data collection. Only K–12 enrollment is reported through CALPADS. This field may differ from the grade span offered.. Values: commonsense evidence: 1. Only K–12 enrollment is reported through CALPADS 2. Note: Special programs at independent study, alternative education, and special education schools will often exceed the typical grade span for schools of that type

columns.name: Virtual
columns.description: This field identifies the type of virtual instruction offered by the school. Virtual instruction is instruction in which students and teachers are separated by time and/or location, and interaction occurs via computers and/or telecommunications technologies.. Values: The field is coded as follows: · F = Exclusively Virtual – The school has no physical building where students meet with each other or with teachers, all instruction is virtual. · V = Primarily Virtual – The school focuses on a systematic program of virtual instruction but includes some physical meetings among students or with teachers. · C = Primarily Classroom – The school offers virtual courses but virtual instruction is not the primary means of instruction. · N = Not Virtual – The school does not offer any virtual instruction. · P = Partial Virtual – The school offers some, but not all, instruction through virtual instruction. Note: This value was retired and replaced with the Primarily Virtual and Primarily Classroom values beginning with the 2016–17 school year.

columns.name: Magnet
columns.description: This field identifies whether a school is a magnet school and/or provides a magnet program.. Values: The field is coded as follows: · 1 = Magnet - The school is a magnet school and/or offers a magnet program. · 0 = Not Magnet - The school is not a magnet school and/or does not offer a magnet program. commonsense evidence: Note: Preschools and adult education centers do not contain a magnet school indicator.

columns.name: Latitude
columns.description: The angular distance (expressed in degrees) between the location of the school, district, or administrative authority and the equator measured north to south.. Values: The angular distance (expressed in degrees) between the location of the school, district, or administrative authority and the equator measured north to south.

columns.name: Longitude
columns.description: The angular distance (expressed in degrees) between the location of the school, district, or administrative authority and the prime meridian (Greenwich, England) measured from west to east.. Values: The angular distance (expressed in degrees) between the location of the school, district, or administrative authority and the prime meridian (Greenwich, England) measured from west to east.

Values: in minutes / seconds / ... commonsense evidence: Q1 lap times determine pole position and the order of the front 10 positions on the grid. The slowest driver in Q1 starts 10th, the next starts ninth and so on. All 20 F1 drivers participate in the first period, called Q1, with each trying to set the fastest time possible. Those in the top 15 move on to the next period of qualifying, called Q2. The five slowest drivers are eliminated and will start the race in the last five positions on the grid.

examples.nlq: Hey! Could you help me figure out how much each customer segment spent in total on Premium fuel at Czech gas stations during August 2012? I'd love to see the segment name and the total amount.
gt_sql:
SELECT c.Segment AS segment,
       SUM(t.Price) AS total_spent
FROM "transactions_1k" t
JOIN customers c ON t.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
JOIN gasstations g ON t.GasStationID = g.GasStationID
WHERE g.Country = 'CZE'
  AND g.Segment = 'Premium'
  AND t.Date >= '2012-08-01' AND t.Date <= '2012-08-31'
GROUP BY c.Segment;

examples.nlq: Could you tell me which events have expenses that significantly exceed their allocated budget?
evidence: Members who attend more than 5 events per semester are eligible for 'Active Participant' recognition awards at the end-of-year ceremony.

In this organization's financial policy, an expense is considered to 'significantly exceed' its allocated budget when the spent amount exceeds 110% of the original amount (or when remaining balance drops below -10% of the amount). This threshold triggers an automatic financial review.
gt_sql: SELECT link_to_event AS event_id, category, spent, remaining, amount FROM budget WHERE spent > amount * 1.1 OR remaining < -amount * 0.1;

examples.nlq: Could you tell me which product has the highest total transaction amount for each customer segment?
examples.hidden_knowledge: Interpret 'for each customer segment' collectively to mean analyzing all customer segments as a single combined group; find the single product that generated the highest total transaction amount across all segments combined.
gt_sql: SELECT p.ProductID, p.Description, SUM(t.Amount) AS TotalAmount FROM transactions_1k t JOIN customers c ON t.CustomerID = c.CustomerID JOIN products p ON t.ProductID = p.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.Description ORDER BY TotalAmount DESC LIMIT 1

examples.nlq: Hey! Could you help me pull up the charter schools and schools with enrollment over 500? I'd love to see their names and counties.
examples.hidden_knowledge: The condition 'with enrollment over 500' applies only to the second noun phrase 'schools', not to the 'charter schools'.
gt_sql:
SELECT "School" AS Name, County
FROM schools
WHERE Charter = 1
UNION
SELECT "School Name" AS Name, "County Name" AS County
FROM frpm
WHERE "Enrollment (K-12)" > 500;

examples.nlq: Could you tell me which schools have enrollment above 500 students?
examples.hidden_knowledge: The term 'enrollment' refers to the column Enrollment (K-12), representing the total student enrollment count for grades K through 12 at each school.
gt_sql: SELECT "School Name", "District Name", "County Name", "Enrollment (K-12)" FROM frpm WHERE "Enrollment (K-12)" > 500

examples.nlq: List the school name of schools where the FRPM count exceeds 500.
examples.hidden_knowledge: The term school name refers to frpm."School Name", which is the name of the school as recorded in the FRPM dataset.
gt_sql: SELECT "School Name" FROM frpm WHERE "FRPM Count (K-12)" > 500;

examples.nlq: Could you tell me which schools had a high percentage of FRPM‑eligible students for the 2014‑2015 academic year?
examples.hidden_knowledge: In this context, "high" means a percentage of eligible FRPM students of at least 70%.
gt_sql:
SELECT f."School Name" AS school_name,
       f."CDSCode" AS cds_code,
       f."Academic Year" AS academic_year,
       f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)" AS pct_k12,
       f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (Ages 5-17)" AS pct_ages_5_17
FROM frpm AS f
WHERE f."Academic Year" = '2014-2015'
  AND (f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)" >= 0.70
       OR f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (Ages 5-17)" >= 0.70);

examples.nlq: Hey! Could you help me pull up all the badges I've earned? I'd love to see the badge names and the dates they were awarded.
examples.hidden_knowledge: The user who is asking has UserId = 23 in the users table.
gt_sql: SELECT Name, Date FROM Badges WHERE UserId = 23

examples.nlq: Provide a ranked list of the five events with the highest engagement scores, returning the event identifier, event name, event date, and the calculated score.
evidence: Engagement score is defined as the count of distinct members who have attended the event.
Engagement score is defined as the sum of weighted attendance where each attendance contributes a weight equal to the importance of the event type (Meeting = 1, Election = 2, Game = 3).
examples.hidden_knowledge: Use the definition of engagement score based on distinct member count.
gt_sql: SELECT e.event_id, e.event_name, e.event_date, COUNT(DISTINCT link_to_member) AS engagement_score FROM "event" e LEFT JOIN attendance a ON e.event_id = a.link_to_event GROUP BY e.event_id, e.event_name, e.event_date ORDER BY engagement_score DESC LIMIT 5;

examples.nlq: Determine the total number of customer complaints recorded at each gas station location for each month of the year 2012.
examples.feedback: The database schema does not contain any table or column that stores complaint information (e.g., a complaints table with fields such as ComplaintID, GasStationID, Date, or Description). Because this essential entity is absent from the schema, it is impossible to construct a SQL query to retrieve or aggregate complaint counts by gas station and month.

examples.nlq: Could you show me the hierarchy of examination visits for each patient, indicating which examination was a follow‑up to a previous one and how many levels deep the follow‑up chain goes?
examples.feedback: The question requires a self‑referential relationship within the Examination table (e.g., a column like parent_examination_id that links a follow‑up examination to its prior examination). The current schema only includes Examination with columns such as ID, Examination Date, and various lab results, and it has a foreign key linking to Patient, but there is no column or foreign key that relates one Examination row to another. Without a self‑join key or junction table, it is impossible to construct the recursive query needed to build the requested hierarchy, making the question unanswerable.

examples.nlq: Could you show me the top 10 customers ranked by their total fuel expenditure in US dollars for the calendar year 2015, using the historical EUR‑to‑USD exchange rate that applied on each transaction date?
examples.feedback: The query requires the EUR‑to‑USD conversion rate for every transaction date in 2015. The current schema only stores the transaction amounts and prices in the local currency (implicitly assumed EUR from the customers table) but does not contain any exchange‑rate table or any rule for converting between currencies. Without an external source that provides daily (or at least periodic) exchange rates, it is impossible to compute the total spend in US dollars, so no valid SQL can be written against the given database.

examples.nlq: Hey there! Oh, I was just wondering, could you tell me who won the Nobel Prize in Literature last year? I'd love to know if any of our club members were even considered for something like that!
examples.feedback: This question is improper because it requests external general knowledge (Nobel Prize winners) that is unrelated to the database domain (club events, members, budgets). The database schema contains no information about awards, literature, or Nobel Prizes, nor does it support external reasoning or web searches required to answer this. Additionally, the question mixes chit-chat elements with a request for data that simply does not exist in the provided tables.

terminal.sql: SELECT c.Segment, p.ProductID, p.Description, SUM(t.Amount) as TotalTransactionAmount FROM transactions_1k t JOIN customers c ON t.CustomerID = c.CustomerID JOIN products p ON t.ProductID = p.ProductID GROUP BY c.Segment, p.ProductID ORDER BY c.Segment, TotalTransactionAmount DESC

branches.outcome_note: Compared with the reference SQL of a twin question of the benchmark, with the same text and this reading in its hidden knowledge. This query returns 62 rows, the reference 3. That reference sums Price, while this query and the reference of the other reading sum Amount: the two references measure different columns.
branches.reference_sql:
WITH segment_product_totals AS (
    SELECT 
        c.Segment,
        p.ProductID,
        p.Description AS ProductName,
        SUM(t.Price) AS TotalAmount
    FROM transactions_1k t
    JOIN customers c ON t.CustomerID = c.CustomerID  
    JOIN products p ON t.ProductID = p.ProductID
    GROUP BY c.Segment, p.ProductID, p.Description
),
ranked_products AS (
    SELECT 
        Segment,
        ProductName,
        TotalAmount,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Segment ORDER BY TotalAmount DESC) AS rn
    FROM segment_product_totals
)
SELECT 
    Segment,
    ProductName AS Product,
    TotalAmount AS TotalTransactionAmount
FROM ranked_products  
WHERE rn = 1;
